name: Reefback

baseline.name: Reefback
baseline.look: Huge slow shelled sea animal carrying living reef gardens.
baseline.ecology: Migrates between feeding grounds; young shelter near warmer shallows.
baseline.limit: Can wreck a careless mooring without aggression; migration changes local currents.
baseline.encounter: Reef tenders post seasonal channels; no riding one as an obedient vehicle.
baseline.scale_note: Adult representative staging envelope; individuals vary by up to 10%. Not shown at common scale on the art plate.

daily: A reefback grazes slowly while smaller fish work around its living shell garden. Turning its heavy body changes the water around pilings even when it never notices a boat.
cycle: Adults migrate between feeding grounds; young use warmer shallows. Reef growth takes years. Storm damage remains visible across later scenes until the calendar supports recovery.
signs: A moving line of reef fish, an unfamiliar current against the tide and a rising shell ridge precede a full silhouette. Coral seen through water can be mistaken for a fixed reef.
escalation: Cruise -> slow turn -> sheltering young -> accidental crush risk. It does not become vindictive after a boat touches its shell.
community: Nacre Quay reef tenders close seasonal channels. Fishers and salvagers dispute lost working hours, and the tide council must explain whose income bears the cost.
scene: Toma can secure a valuable crate only by tying to a living shell garden. Letting the crate go saves the reef and costs a real claim, without the animal rewarding him with treasure.
motion: Keep shell profile and major coral clusters fixed. Use a few massive flipper beats and water parallax; do not make the animal bob like a small pet.
sounds: Water pressure, shell scrape and distant low movement. No obedient transport commands.
rule: A 24 m living habitat. It is neither a convenient mount nor an island that instantly grows new buildings.
canon_status: Additive ecology and production guidance; proposed scene remains unadopted.
